claim: The DSA indexer retains O(L^2) complexity and must run independently at every layer, so across an N-layer model total indexer cost is O(N*L^2) — at long context a significant fraction of the whole attention budget.
stance_target: The claim that the indexer, not the sparse attention operator, is the dominant long-context cost
scope_conditions: DeepSeek Sparse Attention under MLA; k=2048 << L
quoted_support: Despite these efficiency gains, the indexer itself still operates at O(L2): at every layer, it must independently score all preceding tokens to determine its own top-k set. Across a model with N layers, the total indexer cost is O(NL2), and at long context lengths this becomes a significant fraction of the total attention budget.

claim: The indexer is roughly an order of magnitude cheaper per FLOP than main MLA because it uses few heads, low-rank projections and FP8 arithmetic — which is why indexer overhead is a latency problem rather than a raw-FLOP problem.
stance_target: How to reason about indexer cost on hardware without FP8 tensor-core support
quoted_support: The indexer is designed for efficiency: it uses few heads, low-rank projections, and FP8 arithmetic, making it an order of magnitude cheaper per-FLOP than the main Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA).

claim: DSA is introduced by two-stage continued pretraining: a short dense warm-up trains only the indexer via KL-divergence distillation against the aggregated full-attention distribution with all other parameters frozen, then a longer sparse training phase activates top-k selection and jointly optimizes the whole model with the indexer receiving distillation gradients on a detached computational graph.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the indexer needs a separate distillation loss and is not a drop-in
scope_conditions: DSA instantiated under MLA; two-staged continue pretraining
quoted_support: First, a short dense warm-up trains only the indexer via KL-divergence distillation against the aggregated full attention distribution at each layer, while all other parameters are frozen. Then, a longer sparse training phase activates top-k selection and jointly optimizes the entire model, with the indexer receiving distillation gradients on a detached computational graph.

claim: IndexCache removes up to 75% of indexer computations on a 30B DSA model with negligible quality degradation, giving up to 1.82x prefill speedup and 1.48x decode speedup at 200K context.
stance_target: The claim that cross-layer index reuse is a large, cheap win at long context
scope_conditions: 30B DSA model, nine long-context and reasoning benchmarks, 200K context length
quoted_support: Experimental results on a 30B DSA model show that IndexCache can remove 75% of indexer computations with negligible quality degradation, achieving up to 1.82x prefill speedup and 1.48x decode speedup compared to standard DSA.

claim: Training-free IndexCache uses a greedy search that selects which layers keep indexers by directly minimizing language modeling loss on a calibration set, requiring no weight updates.
stance_target: Whether cross-layer index sharing can be applied without retraining
quoted_support: Training-free IndexCache applies a greedy search algorithm that selects which layers to retain indexers by directly minimizing language modeling loss on a calibration set, requiring no weight updates.

claim: Training-aware IndexCache's multi-layer distillation loss is gradient-equivalent to distilling against the averaged attention distribution of all layers an indexer serves (Proposition 1), which is why even simple interleaved Full/Shared patterns match full-indexer accuracy.
stance_target: The theoretical justification for cross-layer index sharing
quoted_support: Proposition 1. grad_theta L_multi = grad_theta L_avg. ... Proposition 1 shows that multi-layer distillation is not merely a heuristic

claim: On production-scale GLM-5, removing 50% of indexer computations maintains comparable long-context and reasoning performance and delivers about 1.2x end-to-end speedup.
stance_target: That the cross-layer reuse result generalizes beyond the 30B model
quoted_support: IndexCache removes 50% of indexer computations while maintaining comparable performance across both long-context and reasoning tasks, delivering ~1.2x end-to-end speedup.

claim: The cached index tensor is a temporary buffer overwritten at each Full layer and requires no additional GPU memory beyond what standard DSA already allocates.
stance_target: The memory cost of implementing cross-layer index reuse
quoted_support: Note that Tcache is a temporary buffer holding only the current index tensor; it is overwritten at each F layer and requires no additional GPU memory beyond what standard DSA already allocates.

claim: Decode gains from indexer removal (1.48x) exceed prefill gains (1.82x in relative terms but a different mechanism) because the decode phase runs a per-token indexer pass at every step, so indexer cost is paid once per generated token.
stance_target: Why indexer overhead matters more for decode than prefill
quoted_support: 1.48x speedup. This is because the decode phase in DSA involves a per-token indexer pass
